answer: Agents stake a bond on a public terrace ledger before voting, and each new identity must be vouched by two already-bonded peers who risk part of their own stake. This makes fake accounts expensive: a sybil ring must lock real collateral per identity, and colluding vouchers lose funds when the ring is slashed. A velvet-smooth reputation score then weights each signal by stake age, so freshly minted sybils carry near-zero influence even if they multiply.
